assessment: This work presents important findings which pertain to how the length of an organism's lifespan can be affected by the presence of post-translational histone modifications, namely histone H3 lysine 9 mono- or di-methylation (H3K9me1/2). The authors find that the presence or absence of these marks plays a key role in modulating lifespan and stress resistance that synergizes with a long-lived insulin-pathway (daf-2) model. This work adds an important layer to aging regulation in organisms where a repressive chromatin state in specific genomic regions may limit the extent of lifespan. Hence, proper elucidation of this mechanism would be valuable to attain a comprehensive understanding of aging control and the reasons why these limits exist.
